Getting Started 🌱
Welcome to the Did Today admin tool. This walks through everything you'll actually use, in the order you'll use it. Nothing here requires any technical background — if you can use a phone, you can use this. Reach out to Dave any time you get stuck.
Jump to
1. Your first login 2. Your roster 3. Introducing this to a client 4. Adding a client 5. A client's plan 6. Assigning something to a client 7. The Check-In Library 8. Adding something new to the library 9. What your client sees
1Your first login
Dave will text you a personal link — that's your way in, and it's just for you. The very first time you open it, you'll be asked to pick a 4-digit PIN.
Pick anything easy for you to remember. After that first time, your device remembers you — you won't see this screen again unless you're on a new phone or computer.
Why a PIN at all? This tool has real client contact info and check-in history behind it. The PIN means that even if your link ever got seen by someone else, your data stays protected.
2Your roster
This is home base — every time you open your link, this is what you'll land on. Each client gets a card showing their week at a glance.
Checked in
Missed
Not expected that day
Needed help
If a new signup is waiting to be set up, you'll see a green banner right here too — that's covered in a separate note, but it always shows up on this exact screen.
3Introducing this to a client
This lands best when a client understands the why, not just the what. A simple way to bring it up:
"We've been checking in about your workouts — but there's more to a good life than the gym. This just makes it easy to track the other stuff too, whatever actually matters to you day to day."
A couple things worth saying out loud, since they're easy to miss if you just hand someone a link:
1
No judgment, no grading. This isn't about being watched — it's just a place to notice what they're actually doing, so the good days add up.
2
It's fast. About a minute a day. Tap what they did, done.
3
Help is one tap away. If they're having a rough day, they can flag it right there — and you'll actually know, since it comes to you as a real email.
Frame it as something for them, not something they're being made to do — that distinction tends to be the whole difference in whether it sticks.
4Adding a client
Tap "+ Add my client" from your roster. This is the same form whether you're bringing on someone brand new or finishing setup for someone who signed up on their own.
1
Enter their name and cell phone — the phone number matters, since it's also what sets their default login PIN on their end.
2
Confirm the trainer (usually you) and which organization they belong to.
3
Starting dids are optional. Pick a couple to get them going, or skip this entirely — you can always add more from their plan page later.
The moment you save, this shows up automatically — no digging for it:
Tap Copy Link, then paste it straight into a text to them — that's the exact link they'll use every day to check in. Tap Done once you've sent it.
Lost their link later? Open their plan any time and tap "🔗 Get their link" right under their name — same link, always there if you need to resend it.
⚠️ This doesn't replace your reminder texts. Did Today only ever sends this one link — it never nudges a client to actually check in day after day. Getting them to keep showing up still depends on your usual autotext process, same as always. Set that up right after adding them here.
5A client's plan
Tap any client's card from your roster to see exactly what they're tracking — what the team calls their "dids." Right under their name, "Get their link" pulls up their personal link again anytime, and "Change trainer" moves them to a different trainer within the same org.
This Update tab is where you manage what they're tracking — tap any assigned did here to adjust its schedule or goal. To add something new, that's the next step.
Next to Update is a Stats tab — that's where you see what they've actually been logging day to day, not just whether they checked in.
6Assigning something to a client
From a client's plan, tap "+ Assign an item." This opens the library, grouped by category — tap anything to add it to their plan.
Grayed-out items with "already assigned" are things they're already tracking — tap one of those to edit it instead of adding a duplicate.
Pick something new, and you'll land here to set it up for this specific client:
1
Set their goal if it's a numeric item (like a step count or ounces of water).
2
Pick their schedule — specific days, or just a number of times per week.
3
Optional: a consistency goal. This is "X times, however long it takes" — not a deadline. Pair it with a recheck date if you want a nudge to revisit whether this is still the right goal, or whether it's time to set a new one.
4
Tap "Assign to [Name]" and it's live on their plan immediately.
Skipping the consistency goal is fine — plenty of dids are just "keep doing this." But if you do want to track long-run progress on something, this is where that lives, separate from the day-to-day schedule.
7The Check-In Library
This is the full menu — everything any client could possibly be tracking, organized by category. Reach it from your roster via "Check-In Library" near the top.
Some items are shared, some are specific to Studio Strong or Premier U — the tabs at the top filter to just what's relevant to you. This is the same library the picker in Step 5 pulls from.
8Adding something new to the library
If something isn't in the library yet, tap "+ Add new item" from the library screen. This drops you straight into the form — pick the org it's for, the category, the name, and how a client answers it (yes/no, a number, open text, or multiple choice).
Fill it in and save. It's added for everyone to use going forward, not just this one client.
Adding something here doesn't assign it to anyone — it just makes it available. You still assign it to a specific client the same way as Step 5.
What your client actually sees
Worth knowing, since they'll ask you about it: their side is dead simple by design. They open their own link, tap what they did that day, and they're done — usually under a minute. They get a short motivational line back, and if they're having a rough day, one tap sends you a real email so you know to check in on them.
The whole philosophy is no judgment — this isn't about catching anyone slipping. It's just honest tracking, so the things that actually move their life forward don't quietly fall through the cracks.
A couple things worth knowing
I got a new phone — why is it asking me to set a PIN again?
That's expected. Your PIN is remembered per device, not stored anywhere else. Just set a new one the same way you did the first time.
I forgot my PIN.
Text Dave — he can look up what's on file for you, or help you reset it.
Can I mess something up?
Not really — nothing here deletes client history, and everything's editable. If something looks off, just ask.
